name: 抄经庐
Copyist's Hut
before: 野地尽头一间茅屋，屋里屋外堆满了书。白发的温夫子伏在案上抄书，手抖得厉害，一笔一笔却很稳。茅屋外围着一伙土兵，为首的捧着一锭银子，说雾驿主请夫子把《茶经》的雾篇交出来。夫子头也不抬：「书是抄给后来人看的，不是卖给雾看的。」土兵们不耐烦了，开始往屋顶上扔火把。

At the end of the open ground stands a thatched hut, books heaped inside and out. White-haired Master Wen bends over his desk copying; his hand shakes badly, yet every stroke comes out steady. Native soldiers ring the hut, their leader holding out an ingot: the Master of the Fog Posts requests the fog chapter of the Classic of Tea. The master doesn't look up. 'Books are copied for those who come after, not sold to the fog.' The soldiers lose patience and start throwing torches onto the roof.
after:
土兵被赶跑，火扑灭了，只烧了一角屋檐。温夫子把一本手抄的册子交给你们，封皮上写着《茶经·雾篇》。他说陆羽的《茶经》十章，他走了一辈子茶路，补上了第十一章：哪座山的茶什么时候采，焙几道火，喝了能熬夜读书，读书人一夜抵得上三夜。「拿去，给你们的学堂用。」

他还说，十年前一个镖头读过这一篇的初稿，只问了一句：「茶能记路吗？」

The soldiers are driven off and the fire put out, with only a corner of the eaves burned. Master Wen hands you a hand-copied volume: The Classic of Tea, Chapter on Fog. Lu Yu wrote ten chapters, he says; he walked the tea road all his life and added an eleventh. Which mountain's tea to pick when, how many firings, and what to drink to study through the night, so that one night's reading is worth three. 'Take it. For your academy.'

Ten years ago, he adds, an escort chief read the first draft and asked only one thing: 'Can tea remember a road?'

name: 云旗滩
Cloud-Banner Shoal
before: 河滩上扎着一支马帮刀客的大营，骡子拴了满滩，刀客们正把从各处劫来的茶砖往船上搬，要顺水运走。这一伙是从雾驿那边过来的，旗子上画着一团云，不跟本地流兵来往，说话也带着东边的口音。

A big camp of caravan swordsmen fills the river shoal, mules tethered all over it, and the swordsmen are loading stolen tea bricks onto boats to float away downstream. This band came from the Fog Posts. Their banner shows a cloud, they don't mix with the local deserters, and they speak with an eastern accent.
after: 大营散了，茶砖卸回岸上。俘虏说他们替雾驿主运茶，雾驿主什么都不缺，就缺好茶，每年要收上千斤：「雾里冷，他说只有茶能叫人记得自己是谁。」船舱里还有一张旧货单，最上面一行写着：「焙茶坊，三百块，半。」

The camp breaks up and the bricks come back ashore. The prisoners say they haul tea for the Master of the Fog Posts. He lacks nothing except good tea, and takes a thousand jin a year. 'It's cold in the fog. He says only tea makes a man remember who he is.' In the hold is an old manifest, its top line reading: 'Tea-firing works. Three hundred bricks. Halves.'

name: 塌埂坡
Broken-Terrace Slope
before: 一面坡上修着一级一级的茶梯田，红土田埂像一道道台阶。一伙兵痞为了取石头修碉楼，把田埂上的石头扒走了好几级。前天一场大雨，上面三级梯田的红土全冲了下来，把底下的茶苗埋了一半。种茶的老汉坐在泥里发呆，兵痞还要他赔「碉楼钱」。

A hillside is cut into tea terraces, their red-earth banks like a staircase. Bullies building a watchtower ripped the stone out of several of the banks. Two days ago a heavy rain brought the red earth of the top three terraces sliding down and buried half the young tea below. The old grower sits dazed in the mud, and the bullies want him to pay for their tower.
after: 兵痞被赶走，石头搬了回来。老汉带着你们重新垒埂，说梯田是把一面坡切成一级级平台，雨水落下来走得慢，土就冲不走；埂一扒，一场大雨就能把红土冲下山，十年也长不回来。阿砚在一旁记下，说夫子讲茶，总是先讲土。

The bullies are driven off and the stones carried back. As you help him rebuild the banks, the old man explains: terraces cut a slope into flat steps, so the rain runs off slowly and can't carry the soil away. Pull out the banks and one big storm washes the red earth off the hill, and ten years won't grow it back. Ayan writes it down. The master always talks about soil before he talks about tea, he says.

name: 头骡关
Lead-Mule Barrier
before: 林中大路被一支马帮刀客的队伍堵住了，他们的头骡戴着红缨、挂着大铜铃，横在路当中，谁也不许超过去。他们的规矩是，茶路上谁的头骡走在前头，谁就是这条路的主人。刀客们拔了刀，说要过，就先把你们的骡子赶到后头去。

A caravan of swordsmen blocks the forest road, their lead mule in red tassels and a big brass bell standing crosswise in the middle, and nobody is allowed to pass it. By their rule, whoever's lead mule walks in front owns the tea road. Blades out: if you want through, first send your mules to the back.
after: 刀客们败了，红缨头骡也被牵到了路边。马锅头不服气，又不敢不服，嘟囔着说：「十年前也有一支马帮不肯让道，头马是一匹青马，比我们的骡子还犟。」他说那支马帮进了雾，那匹青马后来自己回来了，被番人马贩贡布牵走了。

The swordsmen are beaten and their tasselled mule led aside. Their boss is sore but daren't show it. 'Ten years ago another caravan wouldn't give way either,' he grumbles. 'Their lead was a grey horse, more stubborn than our mule.' That caravan went into the fog, he says, and the grey came back on its own later. Gonbu the horse dealer took it in.

name: 马神祠
Horse-God Shrine
before: 林子里有一座小小的马神祠，赶马人出远门前都来这里系一根红布条。一伙流兵占了祠，把马神像搬出来当靶子，把布条扯下来裹脚。看祠的是个哑巴小伙子，被他们按在地上，手里还死死攥着一把布条。

In the wood stands a tiny shrine to the horse god, where muleteers tie a strip of red cloth before a long journey. Deserters have taken it over, using the god's statue for target practice and the red strips for foot-wrappings. The shrine keeper, a mute young man, is pinned to the ground, still clutching a fistful of strips.
after: 流兵被撵走，马神像扶了回去。哑巴小伙子比划着，把攥着的布条一根根系回祠梁上。其中一根很旧，绣着一匹青马和一个「九」字。他指指东边，又做了个骑马回来的手势，再摇摇头。意思是：马回来了，人没回来。

The deserters are driven off and the statue set upright. The mute keeper ties the strips back on the beam one by one, signing as he goes. One is very old, embroidered with a grey horse and the character 'Jiu'. He points east, mimes riding back, then shakes his head. The horse came back. The man didn't.

name: 裁纸坊
Paper-Cutter's Shed
before: 野地里一间破纸坊，老蒲在里头点着灯，一张张地裁纸。他要预备三百张出雾单，等印找回来，一张一张补盖上，簿子就能合上了。一伙兵痞闯进来，以为他印的是银票，抢了一半就跑，老蒲追出去绊了个跟头，还死死抱着剩下的那一半。

In a tumbledown paper shed out on the open ground, Pu sits under a lamp cutting sheets. He's preparing three hundred Out-of-the-Fog forms, so that when he finds his seal he can stamp them one by one and close his books. Bullies burst in, take him for a banknote printer, grab half and run. Pu gives chase, trips flat, and still hangs on to the other half.
after: 兵痞被追了回来，纸一张不少。老蒲把三百张出雾单码得整整齐齐给你们看，每一张上都写好了名字，是照着十年前的簿子抄的。最后一张，名字那一栏空着。「簿子上就是这么写的，三百个，最后一个没写名字。陆镖头说，那个人在后头。」

The bullies are run down and every sheet recovered. Pu stacks the three hundred forms neatly to show you. Each has a name written in, copied from the ledger of ten years ago. On the last, the name box is empty. 'That's how it is in the ledger. Three hundred, and the last one with no name. Chief Lu said that one was coming along behind.'

name: 拓字崖
Rubbing Cliff
before: 山脚一面摩崖，崖上刻着一首前人的茶诗，字有斗大。阿砚趴在崖上拓字，要拓回去给夫子补书。一伙山弩手嫌他碍事，把梯子抽走了，他挂在半崖上下不来，还在喊：「等我拓完这一个字！」

At the mountain foot is a cliff carved with an old tea poem in characters as big as grain measures. Ayan is up on the rock taking rubbings for the master's book. Some crossbowmen found him in the way and took his ladder, and now he's stuck halfway up the cliff, still shouting: 'Wait till I finish this character!'
after: 山弩手被赶走，阿砚连人带拓片被接了下来。诗的最后一句是「一碗喝罢记来路」，落款是前朝一个过雾的茶商。阿砚说，夫子讲过，雾驿主爱茶，是因为茶能叫人想起来路：「他要的不是茶，是让过雾的人别忘了自己从哪儿来。」

The crossbowmen are driven off and Ayan is brought down, rubbings and all. The poem's last line reads: 'One bowl drunk, and you recall the road you came.' It's signed by a tea merchant of the old dynasty who crossed the fog. The master says, Ayan tells you, that the Master of the Fog Posts loves tea because tea makes you remember where you came from. 'It's not the tea he wants. He wants the people crossing the fog not to forget where they came from.'

name: 纸船楼
Paper-Boat Teahouse
before: 河边一座吊脚楼茶馆，四面敞着窗，茶客们一边喝茶一边看雾在河面上走。今天茶馆被一伙马帮刀客围了，他们说老板娘每天往河里放一只纸船，船里装着茶叶，是给雾驿主「送茶」，坏了他们运茶的买卖。老板娘不认，刀客就要拆楼。

A stilt-house teahouse stands by the river, windows open on four sides, its customers sipping as they watch fog wander over the water. Today caravan swordsmen surround it. Every day the landlady floats a paper boat of tea leaves down the river, 'sending tea' to the Master of the Fog Posts, and it's spoiling their tea-hauling business. She denies it, and they mean to tear the place down.
after: 刀客们被打跑，老板娘在窗口又放下一只纸船，船里一撮茶叶，顺着水漂进了雾里。她说这是十年前一个老学究教她的：雾驿主不见人，只收茶，「送过茶的人，雾里不为难」。纸船的船帮上写着两个字：「过客」。

The swordsmen are chased off, and the landlady sets another paper boat on the water from her window, a pinch of tea inside, and it drifts away into the fog. An old scholar taught her ten years ago, she says: the Master of the Fog Posts never shows himself, only accepts tea, and 'the fog goes easy on those who've sent it tea'. On the side of the boat are two words: 'A Traveller.'

name: 茶马司仓
Tea Bureau Store
before: 河边一座高墙大仓，是前朝茶马司的官仓，十年前封了门。如今仓里住着一伙替雾驿看仓的精兵，刀客守门，弩手站墙，谁靠近一步就是一排箭。仓门上贴着雾驿的封条，封条上的日子是丁未年。

A high-walled warehouse by the river, the old Tea and Horse Bureau's official store, sealed ten years ago. Picked troops now live in it, guarding it for the Fog Posts: swordsmen on the gate, crossbowmen on the walls, a volley for anyone who comes one step closer. The Fog Posts' seal strip is pasted across the door, dated the Dingwei year.
after: 官仓的门开了，里面整整齐齐码着茶砖，一架一架都是焙茶坊压的半块。守仓的精兵说，这是雾驿主替千里号存的「回程茶」：「他说那些人回来时要喝，不能叫他们喝陈的，每年换一回新茶。」最里面一架，空着一格。

The store's doors swing open on rack after neat rack of tea bricks, all halves from the tea-firing works. These, say the guards, are the 'homecoming tea' the Master keeps for the Qianli people. 'He says they'll want a drink when they come back, and they're not to drink stale tea, so it's replaced with new every year.' On the innermost rack, one space is empty.

name: 三痕石
Three-Line Stone
before: 林中一处岔道，几块大石围成一圈，石头上落满了马粪和炭灰，是马帮歇脚的老地方。一伙山弩手在石圈里设了伏，凡是牵马路过的，先射马，再抢人。石圈中间一块大青石上，有人用马掌钉划了三道线，一道往东，一道往南，一道往回。

At a fork in the wood a ring of boulders, strewn with dung and ash, marks an old caravan halt. Crossbowmen lie in ambush inside it: anyone leading a horse past, shoot the horse first, then rob the rider. On a big bluestone in the middle, someone has scratched three lines with a horseshoe nail: one east, one south, one back the way you came.
after: 山弩手被打散，石圈清静了。贡布的伙计说，那三道线是十年前千里号划的：往东的是大队要走的雾路，往回的是送信的人，往南的那一道，划得最浅，「像是划的人自己也拿不准」。

The crossbowmen scatter and the ring is quiet again. Gonbu's hand says the Qianli train scratched those lines ten years ago. East was the fog road the main body would take, back was for the messengers. The south line is the shallowest. 'As if whoever cut it wasn't sure either.'

name: 剪尾营
Tail-Croppers' Camp
before: 林子里一座大营，是专偷马的流兵，营里圈着上百匹偷来的马，马尾巴都剪了，免得原主人认出来。偷来的马分三等：好的送去雾驿那边卖，次的留着自己骑，老的杀了吃肉。营里枪手守栏，弩手守林，刀客出去偷。

A big camp in the wood belongs to deserters who do nothing but steal horses. Over a hundred are penned inside, tails cropped so their owners won't know them. Stolen horses come in three grades: the best sold to the Fog Posts, the middling kept for riding, the old ones eaten. Spearmen guard the pens, crossbowmen the woods, and the swordsmen go out stealing.
after: 大营破了，马一匹匹放回林子，认得家的自己跑回去了。马栏上挂着一块木牌，写着买主的话：「雾驿，要青马，别的不要。」流兵头子说雾驿那边每年都来问有没有青马，「像是在找一匹特定的马」。

The camp is broken and the horses let loose into the wood; the ones that know their way home trot off. A wooden board on the pen records the buyer's terms: 'Fog Posts. Greys wanted. Nothing else.' Every year, the deserter chief says, the Fog Posts ask whether he has a grey. 'Like they're looking for one horse in particular.'

name: 讨印林
Seal-Asking Wood
before: 林子里一队土兵拦住了老蒲。老蒲举着他那方入雾印，说自己是茶关的税吏，要见雾驿主。土兵们看了看印，又看了看他腰上那根空印绶，一句话不说，只把竹枪横了过来。老蒲气得直跳脚：「我的印呢？你们雾驿主拿了我的出雾印，就不还了？」

In the wood a troop of native soldiers has stopped Pu. He brandishes his Into-the-Fog seal: he's the tea pass clerk and demands to see the Master of the Fog Posts. The soldiers look at his seal, then at the empty cord on his belt, and without a word lower their bamboo spears across his path. Pu hops with rage. 'Where's my seal? Your Master took my Out seal and he's just going to keep it?'
after: 土兵被你们打退。一个受了伤的土兵说，出雾印挂在他们林中营头的脖子上，营头说那是雾驿主赏的，每有一个人出雾，就盖一下：「可这十年，营头一下也没盖过。雾驿主说了，数没对上，谁也不许出雾。」

You beat the soldiers back. One of the wounded says the Out seal hangs round the neck of their camp captain in the wood, a gift from the Master, to stamp each person who leaves the fog. 'But in ten years the captain hasn't stamped once. The Master said: until the count comes right, nobody leaves the fog.'

name: 茶王树
Tea King Tree
before: 山脚死路尽头长着一棵老茶树，树干要三个人才合抱得过来，说是有一千多岁了，是这条茶路上所有茶树的祖宗。一伙山弩手的精锐守着它，在树下修了碉楼，打算明年开春把它整棵挖走，送给雾驿主当寿礼。树下的老茶农被他们赶走了，天天在山坡上远远地望。

At the end of a blind track at the mountain foot grows an old tea tree so thick it takes three people to circle its trunk. Over a thousand years old, they say, the ancestor of every tea tree on the road. Elite crossbowmen guard it from a tower they've built at its foot; next spring they mean to dig it up whole as a birthday gift for the Master of the Fog Posts. They drove off the old grower who tended it, and every day he stands on the slope watching from afar.
after: 碉楼被你们推倒了，老茶树保住了。老茶农回来，在树根下埋了一包新茶。他说当年温夫子就在这棵树下写完了雾篇的最后一句，镖头陆九也在这棵树下歇过脚，摘了一片叶子含在嘴里，说：「这个味道，以后到了雪山上也认得。」

You pull down the tower and the old tree is saved. The grower comes back and buries a packet of new tea at its roots. It was under this tree, he says, that Master Wen wrote the last line of the fog chapter. Escort chief Lu Jiu rested here too, and put a leaf in his mouth, and said: 'I'll know this taste even up on the snow mountains.'

name: 追信原
Running Letter Plain
before: 野地里阿砚追上了你们，跑得满头是汗，怀里揣着温夫子刚写完的一封信，要你们带给雾驿主。路上一伙兵痞截住了他，以为信里夹着银票，把他按在地上搜身。阿砚死死护着信，嘴里喊：「是茶经！是给雾驿主的茶经！」

Out on the plain Ayan catches up with you, sweating, a letter Master Wen has just finished tucked in his coat for you to take to the Master of the Fog Posts. But bullies have caught him on the way, sure there's a banknote inside, and pinned him to search him. Ayan curls round the letter, yelling: 'It's the Classic of Tea! It's tea writing for the Master of the Fog Posts!'
after: 兵痞被赶走，阿砚把信交给你们。信封上写着「雾驿主亲启」，里面只有一页纸，是《茶经·雾篇》的最后一段：「茶记山，人记路；雾记人，人亦记雾。」阿砚说，夫子讲了，雾驿主数了十年的人，也该有人记一记他了。

The bullies are driven off and Ayan hands you the letter. 'For the Master of the Fog Posts, by his own hand.' Inside is a single page, the last passage of the fog chapter: 'Tea remembers the mountain, people remember the road. The fog remembers people; let people remember the fog too.' The master says, Ayan tells you, that the Master of the Fog Posts has counted people for ten years. It's time someone remembered him.

name: 过蹄道
Per-Hoof Road
before: 去马市的大路上，一伙兵痞拦着赶马人收「过蹄钱」：一个蹄子一个铜板，四个蹄子四个铜板，瘸了一条腿的骡子也照四个算。不交的就把马扣下，牵到路边一字排开，说是「官家征马」。

On the high road to the horse market a gang of bullies is charging muleteers a 'hoof toll': one copper per hoof, four hooves four coppers, and a mule lame in one leg still pays for four. Anyone who won't pay has his animals seized and lined up by the road: 'requisitioned for the crown'.
after: 兵痞被赶走，扣下的马还给了赶马人。一个老赶马人说，马市已经荒了十年，没人敢去：老马官死后，马籍册被人拿走了，没有马籍，买卖就没有凭据，一匹马偷来偷去，谁也说不清是谁的。

The bullies are chased off and the seized animals returned. The horse market has been dead for ten years, an old muleteer tells you, and nobody dares go. When the old horse registrar died, someone took the horse register. Without it no sale has any proof, and a horse stolen back and forth belongs to nobody anyone can name.

name: 数人滩
Headcount Shoal
before: 河边起了雾，雾里站着一排土兵，不拦路，也不抢东西，只是一个一个地数过路的人：「一、二、三……」数完了才放行。数错了就从头再数，一支十几人的马帮被他们来回数了一个时辰。有人不耐烦想冲过去，土兵的竹枪就一齐竖了起来。

Fog has risen by the river, and a row of native soldiers stands in it. They don't block the road or take anything. They count each traveller, one, two, three, and only let them go when the count is done. Get it wrong and they start over; a dozen-strong caravan has been counted back and forth for two hours. When someone tries to push past, every bamboo spear comes up at once.
after: 土兵被打散，丢下一根刻满了道道的竹签。抓到的一个小土兵说，他们是雾驿的人，雾驿主的规矩是凡过雾的都要数，数清楚了报上去：「十年前有一回数出了错，雾驿主到今天也没消气。」

The soldiers scatter, dropping a bamboo tally stick covered in notches. A young one you catch says they serve the Fog Posts, and the Master's rule is to count everyone who crosses and report the number. 'Ten years ago a count came out wrong once. The Master still hasn't got over it.'

name: 青马栏
Grey Horse Stall
before: 山脚下番人马贩贡布的马栏里，几十匹好马都卖光了，只剩一匹老青马，牙口老得掉了一半，没人要。可贡布这几天连一匹马也卖不出去了：一伙马帮刀客放话，谁买他的马，就是跟雾驿过不去。他们要的就是那匹老青马，贡布死活不卖。

In highland horse dealer Gonbu's stall at the mountain foot, dozens of good horses have sold, leaving one old grey with half its teeth gone that nobody wants. Lately Gonbu can't sell anything at all: a band of caravan swordsmen has put it about that anyone who buys from him crosses the Fog Posts. What they want is the old grey, and Gonbu won't sell it at any price.
after: 刀客们被赶跑，贡布的马栏重新开了张。老青马盯着你们看了半天，打了个响鼻，自己走过来，把头往你们的车上一搁，赶都赶不走。贡布叹了口气：「它挑了你们。十年了，它不让任何人骑，只肯驮东西。它认得路，你们跟着它走吧。」

The swordsmen are chased off and Gonbu's stall opens for business again. The old grey studies you a long while, snorts, walks over by itself and rests its head on your cart, and won't be shooed away. Gonbu sighs. 'It's chosen you. Ten years it hasn't let anyone ride it, only carry loads. It knows the road. Go where it takes you.'

name: 白杆林
White-Pole Wood
before: 林中的古道两旁每隔百步立着一根白漆木杆，是给雾天赶路的马帮认路用的。一伙流兵把木杆一根根砍了当柴烧，又在岔路上另立了几根，引着过路的马帮走进他们设伏的山沟。已经有两支马帮在沟里丢了货。

Along the old road through the wood, every hundred paces, stands a white-painted pole for caravans to steer by in the fog. Deserters have been chopping them down for firewood and planting new ones at the forks, luring passing caravans into a gully where they wait in ambush. Two caravans have already lost their loads there.
after: 流兵被打跑，假杆子拔了，真杆子重新立了起来。立杆的老匠人说，雾里认路，靠的是杆，是铃，是马，人眼最不中用。他压低了声音：「雾驿那头也有杆子，只是那头的杆子，每天夜里会自己挪一挪。」

The deserters are beaten off, the false poles pulled up and the true ones replanted. Finding your way in fog, says the old pole-setter, is a matter of poles, bells and horses; human eyes are the least use of all. He lowers his voice. 'There are poles on the Fog Post side too. Only those ones move a little by themselves every night.'

name: 铃匠寨
Bellmaker's Hold
before: 林子里有一户打马铃的铜匠，马帮的铃大半出自他手，每一只铃声音都不同，赶马人隔着雾就能听出是谁家的马队。一伙山弩手把铜匠扣了，逼他打一批跟别家一模一样的铃，好混进马队里偷马。铜匠打一只砸一只，手都砸肿了。

In the wood lives a coppersmith who casts harness bells; most caravans' bells are his work, and no two sound alike, so a muleteer can tell whose train is coming through the fog by ear. Crossbowmen are holding him, ordering bells that sound exactly like other people's so they can slip into a train and steal horses. He casts one and smashes it, casts one and smashes it, until his hands are swollen.
after: 山弩手被打跑，铜匠放了出来。他听见老青马脖子上那只旧铃，愣住了：「这是我十年前给千里号打的，一共三只，声音一只比一只低。」老青马戴的是最低的那只，拴在队伍最后一匹马的脖子上，「是压阵的」。

The crossbowmen are driven off and the coppersmith freed. Then he hears the old bell on the grey's neck and goes still. 'I made that for the Qianli train ten years ago. Three of them, each lower than the last.' The grey wears the lowest, the one hung on the very last horse in the line. 'The rearguard.'

name: 绊索林
Tripwire Wood
before: 林子越走雾越浓，前面的人看不见后面的人。一伙流兵在雾里设了绊马索，专等马队摔倒了来抢。老青马走着走着忽然停下，鼻子贴着地嗅，怎么牵也不走了。前头的雾里传来流兵压低了嗓子的说话声：「来了来了，等马一倒……」

The deeper into the wood, the thicker the fog, until the front of the line can't see the back. Deserters have strung trip ropes through the fog, waiting for a caravan to go down so they can rob it. Suddenly the old grey stops, nose to the ground, and won't be led a step further. From the fog ahead comes a deserter's whisper: 'Here they come. Soon as the horses drop...'
after: 流兵扑了个空，被你们反手包了饺子。老青马绕开了每一道绊马索，像是早就知道在哪儿。它把你们领到一棵老树下，树上钉着一块被雾泡烂了的木牌，只剩几个字：「……号过此，马识途……」老青马在树下站了很久，才肯继续往前走。

The deserters pounce on nothing and you wrap them up from behind. The grey steps round every trip rope as if it knew exactly where they were, then leads you to an old tree with a board nailed to it, rotted by the fog until only a few words remain: '...train passed here. The horse knows the way...' The grey stands under the tree a long time before it will go on.

name: 印匣湾
Seal-Box Eddy
before: 河湾的死水里漂着一只木匣，卡在一堆浮木中间。几个流兵站在岸上，拿竹竿够了半天也够不着，又不敢下水，因为水里有一条大鲶鱼，咬掉过他们一个人的脚趾头。老蒲远远一看就认出来了：「印匣！我的印匣！」

In the still water of a river bend a wooden box floats, wedged among driftwood. A few deserters on the bank have been poking at it with bamboo poles forever without reaching it, and they won't wade in, because a huge catfish lives there that once bit off one of their toes. Pu knows it at a glance from far off. 'My seal box! That's my seal box!'
after: 流兵被赶跑，你们捞上了木匣。匣子是空的，匣底却压着一张字条，是陆九的笔迹：「印到雾驿，借雾驿主一用，盖足了数就还。」老蒲捧着字条，半天才开口：「盖足了数……他到底要盖多少？」

The deserters are chased off and you fish the box out. It's empty, but under the lining is a slip of paper in Lu Jiu's hand: 'The seal has reached the Fog Posts. Lent to the Master for a while; returned when the count is full.' Pu holds the slip a long time before he speaks. 'When the count is full... How many is he going to stamp?'

name: 鹿印营
Deer-Seal Camp
before: 林子里一座土兵大营，营头是个满脸刀疤的汉子，脖子上挂着一方石印，印钮是一只回头的鹿。营里几百个土兵，雾里来，雾里去，见了外人连话也不说。老蒲站在营外大喊：「那是我的印！」营头摸了摸脖子上的印，摇摇头，挥手让土兵放箭。

A large native-soldier camp in the wood, commanded by a man with a face full of scars and a stone seal round his neck, its knob a deer looking back. Hundreds of soldiers, coming and going in the fog, not saying a word to outsiders. Pu stands outside the camp and bellows: 'That's my seal!' The captain touches the seal at his throat, shakes his head, and waves his men to shoot.
after: 大营被你们打散，营头被俘，把印交了出来。老蒲捧着印，手抖得厉害，翻过来一看印面，红泥窑的印泥还在，干了十年。印旁还有一张盖过印的底单，密密麻麻二百九十九个红印。营头说：「雾驿主盖到这里就停了手，说最后一下，得等那个人到了再盖。」

The camp breaks and the captain, taken prisoner, hands over the seal. Pu's hands shake as he holds it. He turns it over: the red clay kiln's paste is still on its face, ten years dry. With it is a stamp sheet crowded with two hundred and ninety-nine red impressions. 'The Master stopped there,' says the captain. 'He said the last stamp has to wait till that person arrives.'

name: 歇蹄店
Rest-Hoof Lodge
before: 老青马领着你们到了山脚一处马帮客栈，自己就往马厩里走，像回了家。可客栈被一伙兵痞占着，马厩里拴的全是他们偷来的马，客房里赌钱的吆喝声震天。老板娘被锁在灶房里，隔着门缝喊：「是那匹青马？它回来了？」

The grey leads you to a caravan inn at the mountain foot and heads straight for the stable, as if coming home. But bullies hold the inn, its stable full of their stolen horses and the guest rooms roaring with gambling. The landlady, locked in the kitchen, calls through the crack of the door: 'Is that the grey? Has it come back?'
after: 兵痞被撵走，老板娘冲出来抱着老青马的脖子哭了一场。她说十年前千里号在这里歇过最后一夜，老青马是镖头的坐骑；后来马自己回来了，在店门口站了一宿，第二天又自己走了，再没回来过：「我还以为它死在雾里了。」

The bullies are thrown out, and the landlady runs out and weeps with her arms round the grey's neck. The Qianli train spent its last night here ten years ago, she says, and the grey was the chief's own mount. Later it came back alone, stood all night at the inn door, and left again the next day, never to return. 'I thought it had died in the fog.'
first: 兵痞的赌桌底下搜出两箱铜钱、一捆马笼头、三十斤青稞面。老板娘拿青稞面给你们烙了一摞饼，说是老青马的接风饭。

Under the gaming tables: two chests of coppers, a bundle of halters and thirty jin of barley flour. The landlady bakes you a stack of flatbreads with the flour. A welcome-home dinner for the grey, she says.
pass: 每次路过，老板娘都给老青马留一槽最好的豆料，也给你们留一锅热汤；她说老青马一来，店里的生意就好。
Every time you pass, the landlady keeps a trough of the best beans for the grey and a pot of hot soup for you. Whenever the grey turns up, she says, business picks up.

name: 看雾婆
Fog-Reader's Hut
before: 山腰上住着一个看雾的老婆婆，马帮进雾前都来问她：今天雾几时起，几时散。一伙土兵把她的小屋围了，说雾驿主有令，不许她再给人看雾。婆婆被困在屋里，隔着窗子还在给你们指：「看见没有？雾都积在谷底，像一碗倒满了的奶。」

Halfway up the mountain lives an old woman who reads the fog, and every caravan asks her before going in: when will it rise today, when will it lift? Native soldiers surround her hut. By order of the Master of the Fog Posts, she is to read no more fog for anyone. Shut inside, she still points out through the window for you: 'See? The fog is all pooled in the valley bottom, like a bowl filled to the brim with milk.'
after: 土兵被打退。婆婆说，晴天没风的夜里，山坡上的地先凉下来，冷气顺着坡往下淌，积在谷底，谷里的水汽一冷就凝成了雾；太阳出来把谷底晒暖了，雾就散了。「雾驿主的兵在雾里厉害，到了晌午就不行了。」她叫你们挑晌午动手。

The soldiers are beaten back. On a clear, still night, the old woman says, the ground on the slopes cools first, and the cold air slides down the hillsides and pools in the valley bottom; the moisture in the valley chills and turns to fog. When the sun comes up and warms the valley, the fog burns away. 'The Master's soldiers are fearsome in the fog. Come noon, they're nothing.' Strike at midday, she tells you.

name: 头雾驿
First Fog Post
before: 河边是九座雾驿里的头一座，一座竹木搭的吊脚楼，楼下拴马，楼上住人，门口挂着一面鼓。如今驿站被一伙兵痞占了，驿卒被赶到河滩上搭草棚，鼓被兵痞拿去装酒。来往的马帮在门口敲门，兵痞就从楼上往下泼洗脚水。

By the river stands the first of the nine Fog Posts, a stilt house of bamboo and timber, horses stabled below, travellers lodged above, a drum hanging by the door. Bullies have taken it. The post-keepers have been driven out to huts on the shoal, the drum is being used as a wine tub, and when caravans knock, the bullies tip their foot-washing water on them from upstairs.
after: 兵痞被扔进了河里，驿卒们回到楼上，把鼓擦干净挂了回去。老驿卒说，九座雾驿本是给过雾的人歇脚、报时的，十年前雾驿主来了，驿站就只管数人，不管歇脚了：「今天总算又能让人歇一歇了。」

The bullies go into the river; the keepers move back upstairs and wipe the drum clean and hang it up again. The nine Fog Posts were built to give people crossing the fog a rest and tell them the hour, the old keeper says. Then ten years ago the Master came, and since then the posts only count people and never rest them. 'Today, at last, someone can rest here again.'
first: 楼里抄出兵痞的存货：糯米酒十坛、火腿六只、一箱蜡烛、一捆蓑衣，还有一面破锣。驿卒说锣是他们自己的，留着雾天报时用。

From the bullies' stores: ten jars of sticky-rice wine, six hams, a crate of candles, a bundle of straw rain capes, and a battered gong. The gong is the post's own, say the keepers; they'll keep it for calling the hours in fog.
pass: 每次路过，驿卒都给你们烧一锅姜汤，敲一通鼓，说是雾驿的老规矩：鼓一响，雾里的人就知道这里有人在等。

Every time you pass, the keepers boil you a pot of ginger broth and beat a roll on the drum. An old Fog Post custom, they say: when the drum sounds, those out in the fog know someone here is waiting for them.

name: 鞍骨洞
Saddle-Bone Cave
before: 林子尽头的山洞里窝着一伙流兵，专偷马鞍。他们把偷来的鞍子剥了皮做靴子，木架拿去烧火，铜饰熔了卖钱。洞口堆着小山一样的鞍架，一伙枪手守在洞口烤火，烤的正是鞍架。

In a cave at the end of the wood lives a gang of deserters who steal saddles. They strip the leather for boots, burn the wooden trees for firewood and melt the brass fittings to sell. Saddle frames are heaped like a small hill at the cave mouth, where spearmen sit warming themselves at a fire made of them.
after: 流兵被赶出洞，好鞍子还给了失主。洞里还压着一摞烧了一半的旧册子，是马市失踪的马籍册：哪匹马、几岁、什么毛色、主人是谁，都记得清清楚楚。有了它，马市就能重开了。

The deserters are driven from the cave and the good saddles returned. Under the heap is a half-burned stack of old books: the horse market's missing register, every horse's age, coat and owner written down clear. With this, the horse market can open again.

name: 六口渔家
Family of Six
before: 河边一户打鱼人家，一家五口，土兵来数了三遍，回回都数出六个。领头的土兵认定多出来的那一个是「雾里跟出来的」，非要带走。当娘的把孩子们挨个搂着数给他们看：一、二、三、四、五。土兵一数，又是六。

A fishing family by the river, five of them. The native soldiers have counted them three times and got six every time. Their leader has decided the extra one 'followed them out of the fog' and must be taken away. The mother hugs her children one by one and counts them for him: one, two, three, four, five. The soldier counts. Six again.
after: 土兵被你们赶跑了。你们数了数，五个人，加上屋檐下蹲着的那条大黄狗，正好六个。打鱼的哭笑不得。可老渔夫说，雾驿的人是真怕数错：「十年前他们数一支马帮，少了一个，雾驿主就把整座驿站的人都罚进了雾里。」

You drive the soldiers off and do your own count: five people, plus the big yellow dog crouched under the eaves. Six. The fisherman doesn't know whether to laugh or cry. But the Fog Post men really are terrified of miscounting, the old man says. 'Ten years ago they counted a mule train and came out one short, and the Master sent the whole post into the fog as punishment.'

name: 三娘鞭
Third Sister's Whip
before: 野地里一伙马帮刀客正在抢另一支马帮，两边的骡子搅成一团，铃铛响成一片。被抢的那支马帮人少，领头的是个年轻女子，头上包着青布，提着一根马鞭，一个人挡在头骡前面，鞭子抽得刀客们直往后退，可架不住人多。

Out in the open a band of caravan swordsmen is robbing another caravan; the two strings of mules are tangled together, bells clanging. The victims are few, led by a young woman in a blue head-cloth with a riding whip, standing alone in front of her lead mule and lashing the swordsmen back. But there are too many of them.
after: 刀客被你们打跑了。女马锅头叫何三娘，丈夫是个马锅头，去年病死在路上，她就接着把这支马帮带了下去：「他答应人家的货，总得有人送到。」她说马市要是开了，她第一个去登记。

You drive the swordsmen off. The woman is He Sanniang. Her husband was a caravan boss who died of fever on the road last year, and she took the caravan over. 'He promised people their goods. Somebody has to deliver them.' If the horse market ever opens, she'll be the first to register.

name: 扣骡卡
Mule-Seizure Post
before: 何三娘的马帮刚到山脚，就被一道卡子拦住了。守卡的流兵说她的头骡是「贼赃」，当场牵走，又扣了她三驮货。那头骡叫黑豆，是她男人生前一手养大的，脖子上挂着他亲手系的铃。没了头骡，后面的骡子一步也不肯走。

He Sanniang's caravan has barely reached the mountain foot when a checkpoint stops it. The deserters on duty declare her lead mule 'stolen property', lead it off on the spot, and keep three loads of her goods for good measure. The mule is called Black Bean; her husband raised it by hand, and the bell round its neck he tied himself. Without the lead mule, the rest won't take a step.
after: 流兵被打退，三驮货抢了回来，黑豆却早被牵进了山里。卡子的木桩上贴着一张条子：「好骡送往山后大营，换雾驿的路引。」何三娘把马鞭往腰里一插：「我去把它要回来。」

You beat the deserters back and recover the three loads, but Black Bean is already gone into the hills. A note pinned to the checkpoint post reads: 'Good mules to the camp behind the mountain, to trade for Fog Post passes.' He Sanniang tucks her whip into her belt. 'I'm going to get it back.'

name: 洗马溪
Horse-Washing Brook
before: 林中小溪边住着一个洗马婆，赶马人出远门前把马牵来让她洗一遍，图个一路平安。几个山弩手把溪水拦了，要洗马的先交钱。老青马一到溪边就不走了，伸着脖子往洗马婆那边够。洗马婆看见它，手里的木瓢掉进了水里。

By a brook in the wood lives the horse-washing woman. Before a long trip, muleteers bring their animals for her to wash, for a safe road. Some crossbowmen have dammed the brook and charge for every wash. At the water's edge the old grey stops and stretches its neck toward her, and when she sees it, the wooden ladle falls from her hand into the stream.
after: 山弩手被赶跑，溪水又流了起来。洗马婆给老青马从头到尾洗了一遍，洗得它直打响鼻。她说十年前镖头牵它来洗过，交代过一句：「它要是自己走回来，替我再洗一回，告诉它，不用再等了。」老青马听完，在溪里站了很久。

The crossbowmen are chased off and the brook runs free. The washing woman washes the grey from nose to tail until it snorts with pleasure. Ten years ago the chief brought it here to be washed, she says, and left a message: 'If it ever walks back on its own, wash it once more for me, and tell it it doesn't have to wait any longer.' When she's said it, the grey stands in the brook for a long, long time.

name: 骡马大集
Great Mule Fair
before: 野地上的骡马大集荒了十年，拴马的石桩还在，马棚塌了一半。一伙马帮刀客和兵痞合伙占了集，谁的马都说是偷的，谁的骡子都要「充公」，好马牵走，劣马高价卖回给原主。马官的衙门被他们拆了，石料拿去垒了自家的马圈。

The great mule and horse fair on the open ground has lain dead for ten years, its stone hitching posts still standing, its stables half collapsed. Caravan swordsmen and bullies have taken it together: every horse is 'stolen', every mule 'confiscated', the good ones led off and the bad ones sold back to their owners at a premium. They tore down the registrar's office and used the stone for their own corrals.
after:
刀客和兵痞被你们一并赶走，大集又热闹起来。凭着找回的马籍册，马市重开了登记，何三娘头一个来报了她的马帮。牧场缺石头垒圈，寨子缺粮，石换粮的买卖开了张。

新马官翻到马籍册丁未年那一页：「千里号，青马一匹，主陆九。」旁边后来添了一行小字：「马归，人未归。」老青马在集口嘶了一声，你们知道，它要往东去了。

Swordsmen and bullies alike are driven out and the fair comes alive again. With the recovered register, the market reopens its books, and He Sanniang is first in line to enter her caravan. The pastures need stone for corrals and the villages need grain; the stone-for-grain trade opens.

The new registrar turns to the Dingwei page: 'Qianli train. One grey horse. Owner: Lu Jiu.' Beside it, added later in a small hand: 'Horse returned. Owner not.' At the fair's gate the old grey whinnies once, and you know: it wants to go east.
